To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PGB domain in the Na+-type stators of the Bacillus subtiilis flagellar motor undergoes a structural transition in the presence of high Na+ concentrations, which is required for the assembly of the stator units.
we visualized the structural transitions of the Na+-type stators in the Bacillus flagellum in response to changes of the NaCl concentration in the environment.
the MotPS complex, a Na+-type ion channel of the Bacillus subtlis flagellar motor, is activated by a Na+-dependent folding and dimerization of the peptidglycan-binding domain of MotS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the activation mechanism of the MotPS motor complex of the flagellar motor.
the mechanism of the bacterial flagellar motor and the mechanism of the MotPS activation process.
the mechanism of the activation process of MotPS in response to Na+.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MotPS complex undergoes a Na+-dependent structural change in which the PGB domain is activated by Na+-induced unfolding and dimer formation.
the Na+-induced dimer formation of MotS-PGB is the structural basis of the activation process of MotPS.
the Na+-induced dimerization of the PGB of MotS, which is the first step of the assembly of the MotPMS complex into a motor, is essential for stator assembly and motor function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Na+ induces the structural transition of the PGB of MotS, which leads to the formation of the dimer of MotPS, and that the dimer of the MotPS is the active form of MotPS.
we have succeeded in visualizing the activation mechanism of the MotPS stator unit of the Bacillus subti lis flagellar motor by using high-speed atomic force microscope imaging.
we revealed the activation process of MotPS complex for stator assembly in Bacillus flagellar motors by high-speed atomic-force microscopy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MotPS complex is assembled into the flagellar motor by means of Na+ ions, which induce structural transitions of the PGB-domain of the MotS subunit.

the MotPS complex undergoes a structural transition of its PGB domains in response to changes of the Na+ concentration and that this structural transition regulates the assembly of the MotSP complex into the flagellar motor.
we observed the structural transition of a membrane protein in real time by high-speed atomic-force microscopy.
